original_question: For the tree of standard Young tableaux ordered by containment, determine whether every automorphism of the underlying unlabeled tree is a composition of transpose automorphisms rooted at symmetric shapes, and whether each node is determined up to transpose by the sequence of rank sizes in the subtree rooted at that node.
target_in_paper: Section 1, Problem 3 (page 1): the open problem on automorphisms of the containment tree SYT of unshifted standard Young tableaux, together with the claim that rooted-subtree rank census should determine a node up to transpose.
correct_elements: Your draft captures the two substantive parts of Problem 3 very closely: it is about the containment tree of standard Young tableaux, asks whether every automorphism of the unlabeled tree is generated by transpose automorphisms attached to symmetric shapes, and asks whether the rooted-subtree rank data determines a node up to transpose.
missing_details: The paper is explicitly about the tree SYT of unshifted standard Young tableaux; this should be stated to distinguish it from the separate shifted analogue in Problem 2.
The tree should be defined as the rooted tree whose structure is generated by containment, i.e. parent and child differ by adding or deleting the largest entry.
The ambient object is the underlying unlabeled tree, meaning the abstract graph obtained after forgetting tableau labels; the question is about graph automorphisms of that tree.
A symmetric shape should be identified as a self-conjugate Young/Ferrers diagram.

The paper treats the transpose automorphisms at symmetric-shape nodes as already known to exist; the open question is whether all automorphisms arise as compositions of these known automorphisms, not whether such automorphisms exist.

A stand-alone formulation should define the transpose automorphism rooted at a tableau T of self-conjugate shape as the automorphism that sends each descendant U in the subtree rooted at T to the transpose tableau U^t and fixes vertices outside that subtree.
The invariant should be stated as the census of the ranks of the rooted subtree, i.e. the sequence c_T(d) giving the number of descendants at each depth d.
The phrase determined up to transpose should be made explicit: if two tableaux T and T' have the same rooted-subtree rank census, then T'=T or T'=T^t.
refined_question: Let SYT be the rooted tree whose vertices are all unshifted standard Young tableaux, with tree structure generated by containment (equivalently, U is a child of T when U is obtained from T by adding one box containing the next largest entry). Regard SYT only as its underlying unlabeled tree. For each tableau T whose Young shape is symmetric, i.e. self-conjugate, the paper notes that there is an automorphism tau_T of this unlabeled tree that sends every vertex U in the subtree rooted at T to its transpose tableau U^t and fixes every vertex outside that subtree. Is every automorphism of the unlabeled tree SYT a composition of these transpose automorphisms tau_T? Moreover, if c_T(d) denotes the cardinality of rank d in the subtree rooted at T (equivalently, the number of descendants of T at distance d), does the sequence (c_T(d)) for d>=0 determine T up to transpose; that is, whenever c_T(d)=c_T'(d) for all d>=0, must T'=T or T'=T^t?
justification: The nearest official formulation is Problem 3 in Section 1. Your draft already matches its two conjectural assertions almost verbatim. The main additions needed for a fully stand-alone, paper-faithful question are: making explicit that the tableaux are unshifted, distinguishing this from the shifted version in Problem 2, defining the unlabeled-tree automorphisms and the symmetric-shape transpose automorphisms, and spelling out that the rooted-subtree invariant is the depth-by-depth census of rank cardinalities. The rewrite stays exactly at the scope of Problem 3 and does not broaden it.
